title: Wound culture
what: A swab is taken from the wound with a sterile stick. The lab grows the germs and checks which medicines work on them.
why: When a wound heals slowly, has pus, is red or painful, or after surgery.
duration: the swab takes 2 to 5 minutes; results usually come in 3 to 7 days
tell_doctor: If you take antibiotics or put antibiotic ointments on the wound
If you are allergic to antiseptic

prepare.title: Ointments
prepare.text: Usually no ointments go on the wound before the swab. Ask your doctor when to do the last dressing change.

prepare.title: Antibiotics
prepare.text: It is best to take the sample before antibiotics. Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor.

prepare.title: Bandage
prepare.text: Do not remove the bandage at home. The nurse will take it off.

steps: The wound is rinsed with a sterile solution
A sterile swab is wiped over the base of the wound
The swab goes into a tube
A new bandage is put on the wound
feel: Touching the wound may hurt. Tell the nurse
after: Care for the wound as your doctor told you
Results usually come in 3 to 7 days
Based on the result, your doctor may change your medicine
red_flags: The wound quickly gets red and swollen, red streaks appear on the skin, or you get a fever: see a doctor the same day
Strong weakness, chills, or confusion: call emergency services

faq.q: Why a culture if treatment has already started?
faq.a: It shows exactly which germ is in the wound and which medicines work on it. That makes treatment more precise.

faq.q: Can I put ointment on the wound before the test?
faq.a: Usually not. The ointment can kill the germs, and the culture will show nothing. Ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Wound culture tomorrow. Do not put ointment on the wound before the test, unless your doctor said otherwise.
